target_customer: Engineering and revenue teams at API, AI and infrastructure companies that bill by usage
problem: Usage based pricing needs reliable, standardized metering of billions of events before billing, and teams rebuilt it in house.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) metering plus managed cloud, usage and seat pricing

founders.name: Peter Marton
founders.background_notes: Worked on Stripe's usage and cost platform.

founders.name: Andras Toth
founders.background_notes: Banzai Cloud was acquired by Cisco.

technical_complexity.rationale: Event ingestion with idempotency via CloudEvents on Kafka, built for millions of events per second; standard distributed systems work with some hard scaling parts.

defensibility.rationale: Apache 2.0 licensed core is easy to copy or fork; stickiness comes from integration into billing pipelines and a community standard.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Kong bought the team in September 2025 rather than building; independent metering players were also consolidated into larger platforms by 2026.

market_need_then: Founders saw at Stripe that metering of usage data lacked standardization across components while usage based pricing spread among API and AI vendors.

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt in November 2023 as Launch of the Day and top developer tool of the week; founder framed open source as a route to standardization.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name with modest developer awareness; Product Hunt launch success but no sourced evidence of broad brand pull.

outcome_analysis: OpenMeter rode the shift to usage based pricing for APIs and AI, with founders who had seen the gap at Stripe. It launched open source in late 2023, raised a $3M seed in March 2024 and was acquired by Kong in September 2025 with its seven person team. The price was not disclosed, so it is an exit of unknown size.
